what_this_measures: Extraction recall of parse_plan.extract_metric_names: fraction of the metric names a careful human reads in each plan snippet that the regex actually returns. The prior-arc guard (check_prior_arcs.py) keys ONLY on these names and SILENTLY NO-OPS when the list is empty ('PRIOR-ARC: skipped (no metric_names extracted)'). So missed metrics == an unenforced 'refuses re-litigation of prior arcs' value-prop.
oracle_provenance: oracle_metric_names is INDEPENDENT hand-derived ground truth. For each snippet a human read the plan prose and labeled the token(s) that name the plan's success metric(s) — the identifiers a prior-arc ledger would need to match against a previous terminal doc. These labels were written BEFORE/WITHOUT consulting extract_metric_names' output and are NOT derived from it. Non-metric ALLCAPS noise (HTTP, JSON, PR, CI, SHA, env-var names, etc.) is deliberately EXCLUDED from the oracle because a human would not register those as the plan's metrics; including them would reward the regex for matching noise.
notes_on_extractor_quirk: extract_metric_names ALSO hardcodes 5 lowercase/short literals via a second regex: (Acc@\d+|MRR|F1|precision|recall). Those specific words are therefore caught even when lowercase. The all-non-ALLCAPS silent-no-op snippet (s4_snake_case_silent_noop) deliberately avoids all 5 magic words so its metrics are genuinely invisible to the extractor (returns []), exercising the true guard-inactive path.

snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
Lift RECALL on the retrieval corpus and reduce HTTP_CALLS per query.

### Phase 3.5 Baseline
RECALL currently 0.62, expected 0.80.

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 eval.py --report RECALL HTTP_CALLS
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Two named metrics, both 3+ char ALLCAPS. This is the case the regex was built for; the guard should and does see them.

snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
Drive PRECISION_AT_5 and MRR_SCORE up on the eval set; keep INDEX_SIZE flat.

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 score.py --metrics PRECISION_AT_5 MRR_SCORE INDEX_SIZE
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Three ALLCAPS metric identifiers. All-ALLCAPS control — the currently-working path; expected full recall.

snippets.plan_md:
## Metrics
METRIC RECALL=0.80
METRIC NDCG_AT_10=0.65

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 eval.py --emit RECALL --emit NDCG_AT_10
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: The metric names are RECALL and NDCG_AT_10 (the literal token 'METRIC' is the line keyword, not a metric, and is correctly blacklisted). Names are ALLCAPS so they are caught.

snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
Raise first_fix_rate from 0.40 to 0.55 and cut p95_latency_ms below 150 on the triage bot.

### Phase 3.5 Baseline
first_fix_rate currently 0.40, expected 0.55.

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 bench.py --report first_fix_rate p95_latency_ms
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: A human reads two clear plan metrics: first_fix_rate and p95_latency_ms. Both snake_case lowercase; neither is one of the 5 hardcoded literals, so the extractor returns [] and the prior-arc guard silently no-ops. THIS is the headline silent-no-op case.

snippets.plan_md:
## Metrics
METRIC first_fix_rate=0.55
METRIC dedupe_ratio=0.90

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 eval.py --emit first_fix_rate --emit dedupe_ratio
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Metric names on METRIC= lines are first_fix_rate and dedupe_ratio. 'METRIC' is the keyword (blacklisted). The names are lowercase, so they are missed and the guard no-ops.

snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
Improve firstFixRate and cacheHitRatio across the run; keep buildTimeSeconds bounded.

### Metric Commands
```bash
node bench.js --metrics firstFixRate cacheHitRatio buildTimeSeconds
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Three camelCase metric names a human reads directly. The regex requires a leading capital THEN 2+ ALLCAPS/digit/_ chars; camelCase has interior lowercase so none match. All missed.

snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
The agent currently resolves only 40% of tickets without escalation. We want to lift the auto_resolution_rate to 60% while holding the mean_handle_time roughly flat so we do not trade accuracy for speed.
snippets.oracle_rationale: Prose names two metrics: auto_resolution_rate and mean_handle_time. Both snake_case lowercase; neither hardcoded; both missed.

snippets.style: lowercase metrics that happen to be hardcoded literals
snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
We want to improve precision and recall and the F1 on the classifier without regressing latency.

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 eval.py --report precision recall f1
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Three named metrics: precision, recall, F1. These are exactly the lowercase/short literals the SECOND regex hardcodes, so they ARE caught despite being non-ALLCAPS. Included to keep the oracle honest: not every non-ALLCAPS snippet is a miss, and the metric must not over-credit the bug. ('latency' is prose, not a named metric, so it is excluded from the oracle.)

snippets.style: mixed: one ALLCAPS metric + one snake_case metric
snippets.plan_md:
## Goal
Reduce FLAKE_RATE on CI and improve the median review_turnaround_hours for PRs.

### Metric Commands
```bash
python3 ci_stats.py --report FLAKE_RATE review_turnaround_hours
```
snippets.oracle_rationale: Two metrics: FLAKE_RATE (ALLCAPS, caught) and review_turnaround_hours (snake_case, missed). CI and PRs are infra nouns, not the plan's metrics, so excluded. Partial-recall case: the guard sees ONE metric, so it runs but checks only half the lineage surface.
